(By Shri Jaideep Sirpurkar - Advocate) And The State Of Madhya Pradesh Through Devendra Kumar Verma, Food Inspector, Food & Drugs Administration, District Raisen (M.P.) .......Res (By Shri Amit Sharma - Government Advocate) -------------------------------------------------------------- Reserved on : 01.02.2024 Pronounced on : 09.02.2024 -------------------------------------------------------------- This petition has been heard and reserved for orders, comi on for pronouncement this day, the Court pronounced the following: Nand Kishore Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80431712/ 1 Signature Not Verified Signed by: Vinod Sharma Signing time: 2/20/2024 1:20:33 Pm -2- Order
texts.facts: The petitioner has preferred this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C for quashing of impugned order dated 07.02.2018 and for discharge along with quashing of case No.300/2011 along with all subsequent proceedings, pending before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Raisen, District Raisen (M.P.). 2. The petitioner was working as Assistant Manager- Quality Assurance with Parle Agro Pvt. Ltd hereinafter referred to as "the Company". The said company is incorporated and registered under the Companies Act, 1956 having its registered at "Off Western Express Highway, Sahar- Chakala Road, Parsiwada, Andheri (East), Mumbai 400099". The aforesaid company is engaged in the business of manufacturing, marketing and distribution of "Ready -To- Serve Juice Based and Synthetic Beverages (Carbonated and Non-Carbonated)" and Packaged Drinking Water, through its various manufacturing plants and sales Offices in India. The aforesaid company had its manufacturing unit in Raisen, hereinafter referred to as "the Plant". The petitioner was posted in the said plant at the time of alleged incident and he was the nominee of the company under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. 3. On 15.07.2006 the Food Inspector appointed under Section 9 of the Act, inspected the plant and drew a sample of loose chemical flavour (orange coloured) powder, which is used as an ingredient in the manufacturing of Frooti, i.e Ready - To- Serve Fruit Beverage, on the basis of suspicion of being adultered. The Food Inspector considered the product to be food item/product. On 17.07.2006 the sample was sent for analysis to the Food Safety Lab, in Bhopal. 4. After a period of more than one month from the date of drawing of sample, the Food Safety Lab, vide analysis report dated 24.08.2006 found the sample to be misbranded and opined that the misbranded ingredients were used by the Company. The Food Inspector after a period of almost 5 years from the date of drawing sample sought sanction for prosecution from the Assistant Controller on 04.12.2010. The Assistant Controller accorded the sanction for prosecution on 14.02.2011. The prosecution was ultimately launched on 18.04.2011 after the lapse of almost 5 years from the date of drawing of sample for the offences under Sections 7(i), 16(1)(a)(i) and 2(xi) of the Act. and the rules framed there under. The complaint was registered as case No.300/2011 and is pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Raisen. On 23.04.2011 the notice was issued and the petitioner appeared before the Court and sought discharge by way of filing application on 09.04.2012 under Section 227 read with Section 245(2) of the Cr.P.C. It was inter-alia pointed out by the petitioner that the sample of chemical flavour could not have been drawn as the same is not the finished product, which is sold independently in the market. It was also pointed out that the prosecution of the petitioner is hit by law of limitation as the complaint was filed after a period of about 5 years from the date of drawing of the sample. With reference to Rule 32(b) of the Rules, the chemical Nand Kishore Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80431712/ 2 flavour is only a flavouring agent and its contents are not required to be disclosed. The contents of the aforesaid chemical flavouring has not come forth even in the report of the Chemical Analyst. Thereafter, the trial Court insisted upon adducing the evidence on 24.08.2016. Thereafter another application was filed seeking discharge on the same grounds. That is how on the next date of hearing i.e. 22.09.2006, trial Court proceeded to frame charges against the petitioner. Against the rejection of the application and framing of charges on 28.11.2016, the petitioner preferred a Revision Petition before the Court of Sessions at Raisen. The trial Court held that the case is an old case and is pending at the stage of consideration of the application for discharge. The Court has to see only a prima facie material on record. The order dated 07.11.2018 was again assailed by the petitioner in the revision before the Court of Sessions. The Revisional Court vide impugned order dated 07.02.2018 dismissed the revision petition on the ground that the sample falls within the defination of food and the same has been found to be misbranded. The Court while dismissing the revision petition has relied upon the ratio of Adalat Prasad Vs. Rooplal Jindal & Others, AIR 2004 SC 4674 i.e. the trial Court has no jurisdiction to recall/review the order. The Revisional Court did not advert to the ground of limitation pointed out by the petitioner. A note appearing in the report of the Public Analyst showed that the loose sample was found in plastic jar. The physical appearance of the sample was orange coloured powder without any taste and odour, alleged to be flavour of indicated material by the Food Inspector. The label was loose sample, having no information about the ingredients inspite of the inquiry made while recording note in the report. The Public Analyst has only opined that no class of flavour indicated as required under Rule 32(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1954. Only on that count, the sample was found to be misbranded.
texts.arguments: 5. Learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently submitted that the sample in question was tested after more than 1 month from the date of drawing of sample. The report of Food Safety Lab indicated that the sample was misbranded. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that the sanction for prosecution was granted on 14.02.2011 and prosecution was launched on 18.04.2011, after a period of more than 5 years from the date of drawing of sample. In terms of Rule 32(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1954, labelling of prepackaged foods shall carry the information in the following manner:- "32(b) Labelling of Prepackaged Foods- Every package of food shall carry the following information on the label:- Nand Kishore Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80431712/ 3 (1) The Name of the Food - The name of the food shall include trade name or description of food contained in the package. [(2) List of Ingredients - Except for single ingredient foods, a list of ingredients shall be declared on the label in the following manner:- (i) the list of ingredients shall contain an appropriate title, such as the term "ingredients"; (ii) the name of ingredients and their weight or volume used in the product at the time of its manufacture shall be listed in descending order; (iii) where an ingredient itself is the product of two or more ingredients, such a compound ingredient shall be declared in the list of ingredients, and shall be accompanied by a list, in brackets, of its ingredients in descending order of weight or volume, as case may be." 6. With reference to the aforesaid requirement the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the chemical flavouring itself is not a food item and is not be consumed independently. Section 468 of Cr.P.C is reproduced hereinunder:- "468. Bar to taking cognizance after lapse of the period of limitation.- ( 1 ) Except as otherwise provided elsewhere in this Code, no Court, shall take cognizance of an offence of the category specified in sub-Section (2), after the expiry Nand Kishore Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80431712/ 4 of the period of limitation. (2) The period of limitation shall be- (a) six months, if the offence is punishable with fine only; (b) one year, if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year; (c) three years, if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding one year but not exceeding three years. [(3) For the purposes of this section, the period of limitation, in relation to offences which may be tried together, shall be determined with reference to the offence which is punishable with the more severe punishment or, as the case may be, the most severe punishment.] 8. As per Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 on the receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub Section 1 to the effect that the article of the food is adultered, the Local Health Authority shall, after the institution of the prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under Section 14(a), forward in such a manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if, it is so desired, either or both of them may make an application to the Court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory.
